extracted.intended_audience: regulated parties and compliance officers (air carriers/operators, aircraft maintenance organizations, immigration officials/schools, SBIC licensees)
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of federal regulatory amendments, airworthiness directives, immigration regulatory changes, and SBIC reporting instructions published in the Federal Register. The page sets procedural requirements, form content rules, compliance schedules, and reporting line-item instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: §212.7(c) — Interview provision for waiver applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The penultimate sentence of paragraph (c) Section 212(e) of §212.7 Waiver of certain grounds of excludability is amended to read: 'The applicant and his spouse may be interviewed by an immigration officer in connection with the application.'

rubrics_metrics.name: §214.3(k) — Issuance of Certificates of Eligibility (Form I-20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance of a student as defined in section 101(a)(15)(F) of the Act for a full course of study at a school which has been approved for attendance by such students, the school shall issue Form I-20, Certificate of Eligibility, to the student. The Form I-20 issued by an approved school system shall designate the particular school within that system which the student will attend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to approved schools and school systems; Form I-20 must clearly designate the specific school the student will attend (not just the system).

rubrics_metrics.name: §319.3/§319.5 — Naturalization: continuous employment abroad and organizational determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: A person of the class described in section 319(c) of the Act shall establish that, at the time of filing the petition for naturalization, he is a person of good moral character, attached to the principles of the Constitution of the United States, and well disposed to the good order and happiness of the United States. §319.5 identifies U.S. nonprofit organizations engaged abroad in disseminating information which significantly promotes U.S. interests (lists organizations determined to qualify).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility under section 319(c) requires continuous employment abroad (see 5-year employment requirement elsewhere) and fulfillment of moral/attachment standards; certain U.S. nonprofit organizations have been formally determined to qualify for section 319(c) benefits (Free Europe, Radio Liberty, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: §319.11 — Procedural requirement for claiming §319(c) benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: The first sentence of §319.11 Procedural requirements is amended to read: 'Persons described in §§319.1, 319.2, and 319.3 shall submit to the Service an application to file a petition for naturalization on Form N-400 in accordance with the instructions contained therein.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimants for §319(c) must use Form N-400 and follow its instructions when filing their petition to invoke the statutory benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form alteration — required allegation (14) statement for §319(c) claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When the benefits of section 319(c) of the Act are claimed, insert in allegation (14) the statement: 'I have been employed continuously for a period of not less than 5 years after a lawful admission for permanent residence, by a U.S. incorporated nonprofit organization recognized by the Attorney General as being principally engaged in conducting abroad through communications media the dissemination of information which significantly promotes U.S. interests abroad and, upon such basis, I claim the benefits of section 319(c), Immigration and Nationality Act.' If not then employed, insert 'My employment terminated within 6 months of the filing of my petition.' Or alternatively, if employed and will continue, insert 'I intend in good faith to resume my residence in the United States immediately upon termination of such employment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are mandatory form statements to be added to allegation (14) when claiming §319(c); choose the alternative phrase appropriate to actual employment status.

rubrics_metrics.name: When notice-and-comment (5 U.S.C. §553) is unnecessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance with the provisions of section 553 of title 5 of the United States Code (notice of proposed rulemaking and delayed effective date) is unnecessary in instances where (examples cited) the amendment relieves restrictions; the addition relates to agency procedure; the amendment merely adds a listing; or the amendments implement a specific Public Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale provided in the order: if a change relieves restrictions, relates only to agency procedure, adds a listing, or implements a statute, the agency may find notice-and-comment and delayed effective dates unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vickers Viscount Models 744/745D/810 AD — inspections and replacement schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Airworthiness directive requires repetitive inspections for cracking and excessive wear of the aileron control rod tubes at wing station 387 and establishes compliance schedules based on hours-in-service thresholds (different requirements for airplanes with ≥12,500 hours and <12,500 hours). Inspections include visual wear-pattern inspection (paragraph (c)), roller clearance check (d), removal and dye-penetrant inspection and diameter measurement (e); replacement required if cracks/holes detected or diameter <1.11 inches (f). Specific interval figures: initial and repetitive inspection windows (e.g., within next 250 hours and thereafter every 500 hours; e inspection within next 2,750 hours and thereafter every 3,000 hours for high-time airplanes; alternate thresholds for lower-time airplanes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspections must be in accordance with British Aircraft Corp. Preliminary Technical Leaflets (PTLs) No. 266 and No. 129 or later ARB-approved or FAA-approved equivalents; measurement tolerances and replacement criteria are specified (minimum/maximum roller clearance 0.005–0.010 inches; replacement required if diameter <1.11 inches); FAA maintenance inspector may approve adjusted intervals upon request with substantiating data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Found Brothers FBA-2C AD — wing-fuselage bolt replacement and wing-root rib inspections
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace the wing-to-fuselage forward attachment NAS 145 bolt with an unused bolt of same part number (or FAA-approved equivalent) within the next 150 hours' time in service after the AD effective date unless already accomplished within the last 350 hours; thereafter at intervals not to exceed 500 hours. Visually inspect wing root ribs repaired per specified Found Brothers repair documents within next 150 hours (unless already done within last 100 hours) and thereafter at intervals not to exceed 250 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement/inspection schedules are mandatory; FAA Chief, Engineering and Manufacturing Branch may increase compliance times upon request with substantiating data. Replacement bolt must be same part number or an FAA-approved equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairchild Hiller F-27/FH-227 AD — inspect and rewire flap drive circuit
rubrics_metrics.description: Require inspection of the flap system motor controller within the next 200 hours' time in service and thereafter at 200-hour intervals; and require rewiring the flap drive circuit within the next 500 hours' time in service (unless already done) in accordance with specified Fairchild Hiller Service Bulletins (or later approved revisions). The inspection requirement may be terminated upon completion of the rewiring requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work must be in accordance with the referenced Service Bulletins or FAA-approved equivalents; FAA Chief, Engineering and Manufacturing Branch may approve equivalent modifications or extend compliance times upon operator request with substantiating data.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Electric CT58 engines — removal schedule for first-stage compressor rotor discs
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise AD 67-1-2 to remove specified GE P/N first stage compressor rotor discs from service according to cycle/hour life limits: discs with more than 10,800 cycles or 2,850 hours on the effective date must be removed prior to accumulation of 200 additional cycles or within next 50 hours whichever occurs first; discs with 10,800 cycles or less (or 2,850 hours or less) must be removed before 11,000 cycles or 2,900 hours whichever occurs first. A 'cycle' is defined as any engine operating sequence involving engine start, at least one acceleration to a power required for takeoff, and shutdown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must track cycles and hours and remove discs according to the stated thresholds to ensure adequate life limit margin; effective date and deficiency rationale included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canadair CL-44D4 AD — inspection and replacement of main landing gear bogie beam
rubrics_metrics.description: Inspect the left and right main landing gear bogie beam P/N 44-87574 for cracks in accordance with Canadair Service Information Circular (SIC) No. 341 (Issue No. 4, dated April 21, 1967) or later FAA-approved revision or equivalent. Remove and replace cracked parts before further flight with same part number or FAA-approved equivalent. Inspect replacement parts prior to installation as specified. Equivalent inspections/parts and SIC revisions must be approved by FAA maintenance inspector or Chief, Engineering and Manufacturing Branch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to each inspection remove foreign matter from the area to be inspected; FAA may approve equivalents and may increase compliance times upon request with substantiating data. This AD supersedes AD 65-11-2 and relaxes some inspection requirements when certain modifications are applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 47 correction — temporary authority to operate (carry pink copy)
rubrics_metrics.description: After an applicant submits an Application for Aircraft Registration under §47.31(a), §47.31(b) requires him to carry the second duplicate copy (pink) on the aircraft as temporary authority to operate it without registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants relying on temporary authority must ensure the pink duplicate is carried in the aircraft as evidence of temporary authority until registration is issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part 151 — runway clear zone definition for Federal aid to airports
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §151.9(b) to reflect the pertinent portion of the description of a runway clear zone formerly prescribed in §77.19(c): a runway clear zone is the innermost part of the runway approach area (standard configuration/length previously in §77.19(c)). The amendment relates to public grants, benefits, and contracts and is made effective immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a definitional substitution (no substantive change) intended to align the runway clear zone description with prior standards for grant/benefit purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIC Annual Report — scope: financings to be reported
rubrics_metrics.description: The report shall reflect all Licensee financings of small business concerns which were outstanding at any time during the preceding 12-month period. If the Licensee has engaged in more than one financing of a single small business concern, each such financing shall be entered in a separate column of the form. Multiple disbursements under a single financing agreement are treated as one financing (one entry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make entries for each financing outstanding during the 12-month period ended March 31; where multiple financings exist for the same SBC, use separate columns and fill full detail for the first financing and limited lines (1,2,7–16) for additional financings of the same SBC.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIC Form — page-level entries required
rubrics_metrics.description: Each page of the report must include: page number and total number of pages; SBIC license number; Employer identification number of the Licensee; Name of Licensee; City, county, and State of Licensee's principal office and ZIP code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee must obtain an EIN if none exists (Form SS-4 filed with appropriate IRS director). Page numbering must reflect total pages (e.g., Page 1 of 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIC Form — entries for each financing (lines 1–16)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each financing outstanding during the 12-month period enter: (1) employer identification number of the small business concern financed; (2) name of the small business concern; (3) address (city, county, State); (4) date business established; (5) form of business (corporation, partnership, proprietorship, etc.); (6) 4-digit SIC code; (7) type of investment and financing (loan, debt security, capital stock, stock rights); (8) put and call features (yes/no); (9) interest rate (or 'N/A' for equity); (10) initial disbursement date; (11) maturity (months) or 'N/A' for equity; (12) total funds disbursed (include discounts, fees); (13) unpaid balance at report date; (14) use of proceeds (code 1–8, with suffix M for marketing or R for R&D when primary); (15) secured (yes/no) where 'fully secured' means collateral value at least equal to amount when made; (16) status of financing (code with detailed options).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more than one financing of same type exists, complete lines 1–16 in separate columns for each financing. In participations, initiating and participating companies each complete lines 1–37 for such financings, but enter only their share on lines 12 and 13. Entries for terms (lines 8,9,11,12) should reflect current terms if they differ from original provisions. Dollar amounts rounded to nearest dollar.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIC Form — use-of-proceeds and status codes (guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use-of-proceeds codes: (1) Operating capital; (2) Plant modernization; (3) Acquisition of all or part of an existing business; (4) Consolidation/refunding; (5) New building/plant construction; (6) Acquisition of machinery and equipment; (7) Land acquisition; (8) Other. If proceeds were primarily for marketing append 'M'; if primarily for R&D append 'R'. Status of financing codes: (1) repayment/recovery of full amount reasonably assured; (2) repayment not assured pending improvement; (3) repayment/ recovery in jeopardy and some loss probable; (4) charged off or disposed of; (5) liquidated through sale/repayment/writeoff/foreclosure (loss absorbed); (6) financing instrument exchanged for another instrument of same SBC prior to reporting date; (7) instrument exchanged through merger etc. for a financing instrument of a different business concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select one code for use of proceeds and one code for financing status. When exchanges/mergers occur, reflect the new instrument in another column of the same report as appropriate and use the indicated codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIC Form — entries for each small business concern (lines 17–37)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete once per financed small business concern (leave blank in columns describing other financings of same SBC): lines 17 & 27 fiscal year end dates (prior and latest); 18 & 28 number of employees; 19 & 29 gross revenue for year; 20 & 30 profit or (loss) for year (exclude tax loss carryovers); 21/31 assets current and total; 22/32 liabilities current and total; 23/33 net worth (deficit); 24/34 inventories; 25/35 receivables; 26/36 borrowings short-term and long-term; 37 SBC discontinuances (code 1–6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter current fiscal year info where available; if current info impossible/misleading due to merger/inactivity/insolvency, see the special handling rubric. Lines 17–37 are completed only once per SBC even if multiple financings exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIC Form — discontinued business (codes) and special handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If the financed small business concern has discontinued business during the reporting period enter one discontinuance code on line 37: (1) Insolvency/bankruptcy; (2) Merger/sale resulting firm eligible for further SBIC financing; (3) Merger/sale resulting firm not eligible for further SBIC financing; (4) Voluntary liquidation (retirement of principal etc.); (5) Involuntary liquidation for reasons other than insolvency (fire, death, condemnation); (6) Other causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter only one discontinuance code or 'N/A' if the concern has not discontinued business. For merged/inactive/insolvent concerns, Licensee may write 'merged', 'inactive', or 'insolvent' on lines 27–36 instead of detailed entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIC Form — verification and signature requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief financial officer of the Licensee shall sign in ink the verification section on the last page of each copy of the report submitted to SBA. The date on which the report is signed and the title of the signer shall be entered in the spaces provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature must be by the CFO; failure to sign or provide date/title may render the report noncompliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIC Form — rounding and numerical entry rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries of all dollar amounts shall be rounded to the nearest dollar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow rounding to nearest dollar consistently across the form; where current info is unavailable or misleading (merged/inactive/insolvent) the prescribed word may be used instead of numerical entries on lines 27–36.
